purpose: Define the smallest trust boundary that turns untrusted request identifiers into an authorization command derived only from server-owned authentication evidence and route authorization bindings.

definitions.meaning: An opaque inbound identifier that has no authentication authority until a trusted server-side resolver returns exactly one matching trusted session-evidence row.
A server-resolved record binding one authentication evidence reference to one non-empty session identity and an explicit trust result.
A server-owned record binding one route identity to the exact required resource, action, scope, and scope-evidence reference for authorization.
The internal request identity, authenticated session identity, required permission, and trusted scope-evidence reference passed to the authorization decision service.
The property that every authorization-command value exactly matches either the inbound request identity or the unique matching trusted resolver rows from which it must be derived.
Exactly one trusted authentication row and exactly one complete route binding match non-empty inbound identifiers, and the candidate authorization command has exact provenance from those rows.
The authorization command passed every command-boundary Rule and may be evaluated by the existing authorization service.
The boundary did not establish exact trusted command provenance; no downstream authorization call is permitted.

claim_limit: User-directed candidate definitions for local implementation and review; they are not admitted canonical definitions and grant no acceptance, publication, deployment, or production authority.
